purpose: Prepare interns to build, evaluate, document, deploy, monitor, and govern reproducible machine-learning systems safely under human supervision.
global_rules: Treat datasets as sensitive unless marked public; never scrape or expose personal/client data.
Keep train/validation/test separation honest and prevent preprocessing leakage.
Use approved tools, datasets, accounts, compute, and licences; require approval for production or paid services.
Make results reproducible with versions, seeds, data references, tests, and independent verification.
Document bias, privacy, security, uncertainty, limitations, failures, time, and AI assistance honestly.

days.phase: ML Workflow, Environment, Ethics, and Reproducibility
days.topic: ML Workflow and Environment
days.objective: Configure and verify an approved Python, Jupyter, pandas, and scikit-learn environment; create a reproducible project structure; run a synthetic-data baseline; and prove honest train/test separation.
learning_outcomes: Explain ML Workflow and Environment clearly to a technical supervisor.
Use Python, Jupyter, pandas safely within the approved ML workflow.

Produce reproducible, measurable evidence for: Configure and verify an approved Python, Jupyter, pandas, and scikit-learn environment; create a reproducible project structure; run a synthetic-data baseline; and prove honest train/test separation.
Evaluate data quality, leakage, performance, bias/privacy risk, and limitations with human oversight.
core_concepts: ML Workflow, Environment, Ethics, and Reproducibility
practical_procedure: Confirm the written objective, authorized dataset, licence, privacy classification, computing boundary, supervisor approvals, and stop conditions.
Create the day folder with data/raw, data/processed, notebooks, src, tests, models, output, evidence, and report; never overwrite prior evidence.
Record OS, Python, package, seed, dataset version/hash, hardware, and tools: Python, Jupyter, pandas, scikit-learn.
Frame the prediction or analysis task, target population, features, label, intended user, baseline, metric, acceptance threshold, and harmful misuse to avoid.
Inspect data quality before modeling; check schema, missingness, duplicates, ranges, imbalance, representativeness, provenance, and leakage risks.

Implement the practical objective: Configure and verify an approved Python, Jupyter, pandas, and scikit-learn environment; create a reproducible project structure; run a synthetic-data baseline; and prove honest train/test separation.
Evaluate on untouched validation/test data with appropriate metrics, slice analysis, errors, uncertainty, and comparison to the baseline or heuristic.
Independently verify by a clean rerun from saved dependencies and seeds plus a unit test, alternate calculation, peer review, or supervisor check.
Save privacy-reviewed evidence, model/data documentation, troubleshooting, limitations, restoration/cleanup record, and an honest AI/tool-assistance disclosure.
safety_ethics_and_beyond_lab_rules: Treat datasets as sensitive unless explicitly marked public; do not scrape personal data or upload protected data to public AI/cloud services.
Keep train, validation, and test separation honest. Fit preprocessing only on training data and document all leakage checks.
Use only approved local/open tools, datasets, accounts, compute, and licences. Obtain supervisor approval before paid services, production changes, or external deployment.
Do not expose secrets, identifiers, personal/client records, notifications, or proprietary model/data details in code, repositories, screenshots, prompts, or reports.
Record seeds, versions, assumptions, metrics, subgroup results, failures, time, uncertainty, and limitations honestly. Never invent performance or hide negative results.
Disclose AI/tool assistance, verify generated code and claims, preserve human oversight, and stop/escalate if authorization, safety, fairness, privacy, or ownership is unclear.
self_check_questions: Can you explain ML Workflow and Environment in under two minutes without notes?
What evidence proves the result is reproducible rather than copied or accidental?
How did you prevent data leakage and preserve an untouched evaluation set?
Why is the chosen metric appropriate, and which harmful errors can it hide?
Which data quality, bias, privacy, security, or misuse risk is most important today?
What did the independent verification show, and what would you troubleshoot first before review?
Is this ready for real use? State the limitations, required human oversight, and next approval.

evidence_checklist.requirement: Privacy-reviewed screenshot of the authorized environment, versions, dataset reference, and safe starting state.
Reproducible source, notebook, tests, configuration, requirements/lockfile, and outputs; no secrets or restricted data.
Baseline and model metrics, split description, slice/error analysis, acceptance decision, and limitations.
Clean-rerun result and independent test, alternate calculation, peer review, or supervisor sign-off.
Professional report with scope, data statement, method, results, responsible-ML controls, troubleshooting, disclosure, and references.

learning_outcomes: Explain Monitoring, Governance, Security, and Responsible ML: Assessment and Professional Report clearly to a technical supervisor.
Use Evidently optional, MLflow local, NIST AI RMF safely within the approved ML workflow.

Produce reproducible, measurable evidence for: Apply Monitoring, Governance, Security, and Responsible ML: Assessment and Professional Report to an approved public or synthetic dataset, measure the result against a documented baseline and acceptance criterion, independently verify it, and explain limitations in a professional technical report.
Evaluate data quality, leakage, performance, bias/privacy risk, and limitations with human oversight.
core_concepts: Monitoring, Governance, Security, and Responsible ML
data drift concept drift and performance monitoring
fairness privacy security and adversarial risks
model cards risk assessments and approval
incident response retraining retirement and audit evidence
practical_procedure: Confirm the written objective, authorized dataset, licence, privacy classification, computing boundary, supervisor approvals, and stop conditions.
Create the day folder with data/raw, data/processed, notebooks, src, tests, models, output, evidence, and report; never overwrite prior evidence.
Record OS, Python, package, seed, dataset version/hash, hardware, and tools: Evidently optional, MLflow local, NIST AI RMF, Git.
Frame the prediction or analysis task, target population, features, label, intended user, baseline, metric, acceptance threshold, and harmful misuse to avoid.
Inspect data quality before modeling; check schema, missingness, duplicates, ranges, imbalance, representativeness, provenance, and leakage risks.

Implement the practical objective: Apply Monitoring, Governance, Security, and Responsible ML: Assessment and Professional Report to an approved public or synthetic dataset, measure the result against a documented baseline and acceptance criterion, independently verify it, and explain limitations in a professional technical report.
Evaluate on untouched validation/test data with appropriate metrics, slice analysis, errors, uncertainty, and comparison to the baseline or heuristic.
Independently verify by a clean rerun from saved dependencies and seeds plus a unit test, alternate calculation, peer review, or supervisor check.
Save privacy-reviewed evidence, model/data documentation, troubleshooting, limitations, restoration/cleanup record, and an honest AI/tool-assistance disclosure.
safety_ethics_and_beyond_lab_rules: Treat datasets as sensitive unless explicitly marked public; do not scrape personal data or upload protected data to public AI/cloud services.
Keep train, validation, and test separation honest. Fit preprocessing only on training data and document all leakage checks.
Use only approved local/open tools, datasets, accounts, compute, and licences. Obtain supervisor approval before paid services, production changes, or external deployment.
Do not expose secrets, identifiers, personal/client records, notifications, or proprietary model/data details in code, repositories, screenshots, prompts, or reports.
Record seeds, versions, assumptions, metrics, subgroup results, failures, time, uncertainty, and limitations honestly. Never invent performance or hide negative results.
Disclose AI/tool assistance, verify generated code and claims, preserve human oversight, and stop/escalate if authorization, safety, fairness, privacy, or ownership is unclear.
self_check_questions: Can you explain Monitoring, Governance, Security, and Responsible ML: Assessment and Professional Report in under two minutes without notes?
What evidence proves the result is reproducible rather than copied or accidental?
How did you prevent data leakage and preserve an untouched evaluation set?
Why is the chosen metric appropriate, and which harmful errors can it hide?
Which data quality, bias, privacy, security, or misuse risk is most important today?
What did the independent verification show, and what would you troubleshoot first before review?
Is this ready for real use? State the limitations, required human oversight, and next approval.

evidence_checklist.requirement: Privacy-reviewed screenshot of the authorized environment, versions, dataset reference, and safe starting state.
Reproducible source, notebook, tests, configuration, requirements/lockfile, and outputs; no secrets or restricted data.
Baseline and model metrics, split description, slice/error analysis, acceptance decision, and limitations.
Clean-rerun result and independent test, alternate calculation, peer review, or supervisor sign-off.
Professional report with scope, data statement, method, results, responsible-ML controls, troubleshooting, disclosure, and references.

days.required_submission: Baseline screenshot, reproducible project, evaluation evidence, independent verification, responsible-ML check, and professional report.
days.prerequisite: Completion of Day 169; unresolved data, environment, ethics, evaluation, or restoration issues must be escalated first.
report_sections: Objective, scope, authorization, and intended use
Dataset statement, provenance, licence, and privacy
Metrics, results, slice/error analysis, and uncertainty
Bias, privacy, security, ethics, and human oversight
Conclusion, deployment boundary, and next approval

Disclose AI/tool assistance, verify generated code and claims, preserve human oversight, and stop/escalate if authorization, safety, fairness, privacy, or ownership is unclear.
